/-!
# Erdős Problem 645

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/645](https://www.erdosproblems.com/645)
- [BrLa99] Brown, Tom C. and Landman, Bruce M., Monochromatic arithmetic progressions with large
  differences. Bull. Austral. Math. Soc. (1999), 21--35.
-/

@[expose] public section


namespace Erdos645

/--
If ℕ is $2$-coloured then there must exist a monochromatic three-term arithmetic progression
$x,x+d,x+2d$ such that $d>x$.

This was first proved by Brown and Landman [BrLa99], who in fact show that this is always possible
with $d>f(x)$ for any increasing function $f$.

This was formalized in Lean by Alexeev using Aristotle and ChatGPT.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.24.0/ErdosProblems/Erdos645.lean"]
theorem erdos_645 (c : ℕ → Bool) : ∃ x d, 0 < x ∧ x < d ∧
    (∃ C, c x = C ∧ c (x + d) = C ∧ c (x + 2 * d) = C) := by
  sorry

end Erdos645

reformulations.difference: The source asks a yes/no question ('must there exist ...?'), and its recorded answer is yes. The Lean states the affirmative claim directly as a theorem, not as `answer(True) ↔ P`. The Lean also colours all of ℕ (including 0) by `c : ℕ → Bool` and requires `0 < x`, where Erdős and Brown–Landman colour the positive integers. 'Monochromatic' is written as `∃ C, c x = C ∧ c (x+d) = C ∧ c (x+2d) = C`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: (1) `answer(True) ↔ P` is `True ↔ P`, which is equivalent to `P`. (2) Colourings of ℕ+ and colourings of ℕ restricted to x > 0 give the same claim. Every term x, x+d, x+2d is positive because d > x > 0, so the colour of 0 never matters. A colouring of ℕ+ extends to ℕ by colouring 0 arbitrarily, and a colouring of ℕ restricts to ℕ+. (3) Reading ℕ as containing 0, so that x = 0 is allowed, also gives the same claim. Given c, apply the x ≥ 0 version to c'(n) = c(2n+1); a progression x', x'+d', x'+2d' with d' > x' gives the progression 2x'+1, 2x'+1+2d', 2x'+1+4d' for c, and 2d' ≥ 2x'+2 > 2x'+1. (4) The `∃ C` form is equivalent to c x = c(x+d) = c(x+2d). All three equivalences (Lean ↔ ℕ+ version, Lean ↔ x ≥ 0 version, (True ↔ P) ↔ P) compile without errors in /workspace/review/equiv.lean, together with `rfl` checks that P is exactly the theorem's type.

review.notes:
I found no misformalization. The single theorem `Erdos645.erdos_645` states exactly the problem posed on erdosproblems.com/645 and in Erdős's original text (Ann. Discrete Math. 6 (1980), p. 93: 'Is it true that if we divide the integers into two classes then there always is a three term arithmetic progression all whose elements are in the same class and whose difference is larger than its first term?'). The statement uses no non-standard definitions, only ℕ, Bool, `<`, `+` and `*`.

Status: `research solved` with `formal_proof using lean4` matches the source's 'PROVED (LEAN) — solved in the affirmative'. The teorth/erdosproblems data agrees ('proved (Lean)').

The linked proof (plby/lean-proofs, written for Lean v4.24.0) ends with a theorem whose statement is textually identical to the FC one. I compiled it against this checkout's Mathlib (Lean v4.33.1) after replacing two broken automation steps (`bound; induction … <;> aesop` became an explicit `Nat.le_induction`; `bound; exact?` became an explicit call to `case_2_inductive`). It then compiles without `sorry` and uses only `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`. An `example` confirmed that its type is exactly `type_of% @Erdos645.erdos_645`.

The docstrings match the source. The remark that Brown–Landman get $d>f(x)$ 'for any increasing function $f$' is copied from erdosproblems.com; the paper's abstract (bounds for $w(f,3,2)$, with $d \ge f(a)$ for $f:\mathbb{Z}^+\to\mathbb{R}^+$) is consistent with it, but I did not read the full paper.

The file states the affirmative directly rather than using the repository's preferred `answer(True) ↔ …` style for questions. This is a style matter and is mathematically equivalent; I recorded it only as a reformulation.

erdosproblems.com returns a Cloudflare 403 to curl, so I read the page through the r.jina.ai reader proxy and rebuilt the LaTeX from the MathJax `data-latex` attributes.

`git status` shows `lakefile.toml` as modified and `run/` as untracked in the checkout. Both are timestamped 12:21, before this review began, so they come from the sandbox setup. The reviewed file is identical to commit aea251bb.
